policy: Reviewed native CLI help output. Hostname defaults are normalized.

cases.stdout:
Usage: gridstator [options] [command]

Gridstator: multiple machines, one workflow. Run builds and tests on your LAN
cluster.

Options:
  -v, --version               output the version number
  -h, --help                  display help for command

Commands:
  login [options] <url>       Connect this machine to a controller (verifies the
                              CA fingerprint and token)
  status [options]            Show cluster, node and job summary
  nodes [options]             List and manage worker nodes
  jobs [options]              List jobs (most recent first)
  job [options] <id>          Show details of one job
  run [options] [command...]  Run a command in a container on a cluster node,
                              against a snapshot of this project
  logs [options] <id>         Print a job's logs
  cancel <id>                 Cancel a queued or running job
  retry [options] <id>        Run a finished job again with the same snapshot
                              and settings
  snapshot [options]          Capture this project as a snapshot and upload it
                              (shows what would be sent)
  token                       Manage client and join tokens (admin)
  groups [options]            List job groups (sharded runs), most recent first
  group                       Inspect and control a job group (sharded run)
  init [options]              Create a gridstator.yml in the current project
  agents                      Keep worker agents on the controller’s build
                              (status, updates, auto-update)
  build [options] [context]   Build a Docker image from this project on a
                              cluster node (BuildKit)
  actions                     Run GitHub Actions workflows on the cluster with
                              act
  artifacts [options] <id>    List or download the artifacts of a job
  doctor [options]            Check this machine's setup and the connection to
                              the controller
  controller                  Run and manage the cluster controller
  agent                       Run a worker agent on this machine
  help [command]              display help for command

Usage: gridstator login [options] <url>

Connect this machine to a controller (verifies the CA fingerprint and token)

Arguments:
  url                     controller URL, e.g. https://192.168.1.20:7300

Options:
  --fingerprint <sha256>  cluster CA fingerprint (printed by `controller init`)
  --token <token>         client token (from `gridstator token create`)
  -h, --help              display help for command

Usage: gridstator status [options]

Show cluster, node and job summary

Options:
  --json      machine-readable output
  -h, --help  display help for command

Usage: gridstator nodes [options] [command]

List and manage worker nodes

Options:
  --json                   machine-readable output
  -h, --help               display help for command

Commands:
  show [options] <node>
  set [options] <node>     Rename a node or change its scheduling settings
  enable <node>            Allow the scheduler to place jobs on a node
  disable <node>           Stop placing new jobs on a node (running jobs
                           continue)
  drain <node>             Stop placing new jobs on a node and let running jobs
                           finish
  remove [options] <node>  Remove a node and revoke its credential (admin)

Usage: gridstator nodes show [options] <node>

Arguments:
  node        node name or id

Options:
  --json      machine-readable output
  -h, --help  display help for command

Usage: gridstator nodes set [options] <node>

Rename a node or change its scheduling settings

Arguments:
  node                     node name or id

Options:
  --name <name>            change the worker name without changing its identity
  --max-concurrency <n>    maximum concurrent jobs
  --reserve-cpus <n>       CPUs held back for the host
  --reserve-memory <size>  memory held back for the host, e.g. 8g
  --labels <list>          replace labels (comma-separated; empty string clears)
  -h, --help               display help for command

Usage: gridstator nodes enable [options] <node>

Allow the scheduler to place jobs on a node

Arguments:
  node        node name or id

Options:
  -h, --help  display help for command

Usage: gridstator nodes disable [options] <node>

Stop placing new jobs on a node (running jobs continue)

Arguments:
  node        node name or id

Options:
  -h, --help  display help for command

Usage: gridstator nodes drain [options] <node>

Stop placing new jobs on a node and let running jobs finish

Arguments:
  node        node name or id

Options:
  -h, --help  display help for command

Usage: gridstator nodes remove [options] <node>

Remove a node and revoke its credential (admin)

Arguments:
  node        node name or id

Options:
  --force     cancel jobs still running on the node
  -h, --help  display help for command

Usage: gridstator jobs [options]

List jobs (most recent first)

Options:
  --state <states>  filter by state (comma-separated: created, queued, assigned,
                    starting, running, succeeded, failed, cancelled, lost)
  --node <node>     filter by node
  --limit <n>       maximum number of jobs (default: "30")
  --json            machine-readable output
  -h, --help        display help for command

Usage: gridstator job [options] <id>

Show details of one job

Arguments:
  id          job id

Options:
  --json      machine-readable output
  -h, --help  display help for command

Usage: gridstator run [options] [command...]

Run a command in a container on a cluster node, against a snapshot of this
project

Arguments:
  command                  command to run (after --). A single argument is run
                           with sh -c

Options:
  -t, --task <name>        run a task defined in gridstator.yml
  --image <image>          container image (default from gridstator.yml, else
                           node:24-bookworm)
  --node <node>            run on this node (name or id)
  -l, --label <label>      require a node label (repeatable) (default: [])
  --cpus <n>               CPUs to reserve and limit the container to
  --memory <size>          memory to reserve and limit the container to, e.g. 4g
  -e, --env <NAME=value>   environment variable (repeatable) (default: [])
  -s, --secret-env <NAME>  forward a secret from this shell; masked in logs
                           (repeatable) (default: [])
  --timeout <duration>     stop the job after this long, e.g. 30m
  --priority <n>           higher runs first (-100..100)
  --retries <n>            automatic retries if the node is lost
  --name <name>            display name for the job
  --shell                  run the arguments as one shell command (sh -c)
  -a, --artifact <path>    collect a file or directory as an artifact after the
                           run (repeatable) (default: [])
  --shards <n>             split into N parallel shards across workers; use
                           {shard} and {total} in the command
  --prefer <node>          prefer this worker when it can take the job
                           (repeatable) (default: [])
  --no-snapshot            do not send the project; run in an empty /workspace
  -d, --detach             print the job id and exit instead of streaming logs
  --json                   print the submitted job as JSON (implies --detach)
  -h, --help               display help for command

Usage: gridstator logs [options] <id>

Print a job's logs

Arguments:
  id            job id

Options:
  -f, --follow  keep streaming until the job finishes
  --json        print log entries as JSON lines
  -h, --help    display help for command

Usage: gridstator cancel [options] <id>

Cancel a queued or running job

Arguments:
  id          job id

Options:
  -h, --help  display help for command

Usage: gridstator retry [options] <id>

Run a finished job again with the same snapshot and settings

Arguments:
  id            job id

Options:
  -d, --detach  print the new job id and exit
  -h, --help    display help for command

Usage: gridstator snapshot [options]

Capture this project as a snapshot and upload it (shows what would be sent)

Options:
  --dry-run   capture only; do not upload
  --json      machine-readable output including the full file list
  -h, --help  display help for command

Usage: gridstator token [options] [command]

Manage client and join tokens (admin)

Options:
  -h, --help        display help for command

Commands:
  create [options]  Create a client token, or a join token for adding a worker
  list [options]
  revoke <id>
  help [command]    display help for command

Usage: gridstator token create [options]

Create a client token, or a join token for adding a worker

Options:
  --join            create a join token for `gridstator agent join`
  --name <name>     token name (shown in job ownership and audit records)
  --role <role>     client token role: operator or admin (default: "operator")
  --ttl <duration>  expiry, e.g. 24h (join tokens default to 24h; client tokens
                    never expire)
  --uses <n>        join token: number of agents that may use it (default: "1")
  --json            machine-readable output
  -h, --help        display help for command

Usage: gridstator token list [options]

Options:
  --json      machine-readable output
  -h, --help  display help for command

Usage: gridstator token revoke [options] <id>

Arguments:
  id          token id (from `gridstator token list`)

Options:
  -h, --help  display help for command

Usage: gridstator groups [options]

List job groups (sharded runs), most recent first

Options:
  --limit <n>  maximum number of groups (default: "20")
  --json       machine-readable output
  -h, --help   display help for command

Usage: gridstator group [options] [command]

Inspect and control a job group (sharded run)

Options:
  -h, --help            display help for command

Commands:
  show [options] <id>
  cancel <id>
  retry [options] <id>  Run the shards that failed, were lost or were cancelled
                        again
  help [command]        display help for command

Usage: gridstator group show [options] <id>

Arguments:
  id          group id

Options:
  --json      machine-readable output (includes combined test results)
  -h, --help  display help for command

Usage: gridstator group cancel [options] <id>

Arguments:
  id          group id

Options:
  -h, --help  display help for command

Usage: gridstator group retry [options] <id>

Run the shards that failed, were lost or were cancelled again

Arguments:
  id            group id

Options:
  -d, --detach  do not stream logs
  -h, --help    display help for command

Usage: gridstator init [options]

Create a gridstator.yml in the current project

Options:
  --force     overwrite an existing gridstator.yml
  -h, --help  display help for command

Usage: gridstator agents [options] [command]

Keep worker agents on the controller’s build (status, updates, auto-update)

Options:
  -h, --help                   display help for command

Commands:
  status [options]             Show which workers run the controller’s build
  update [options] [nodes...]  Update workers to the controller’s build, one at
                               a time: drain, update, wait until it is back
                               (admin)
  cancel                       Stop the running rollout; the worker being
                               updated right now finishes (admin)
  set [options] [node]         Set auto-update and toolchain options: for one
                               worker, or the cluster default (no node)
  help [command]               display help for command

Usage: gridstator agents status [options]

Show which workers run the controller’s build

Options:
  --json      machine-readable output
  --check     exit with code 3 if a reachable worker is not on the controller’s
              build (offline workers do not count)
  -h, --help  display help for command

Usage: gridstator agents update [options] [nodes...]

Update workers to the controller’s build, one at a time: drain, update, wait
until it is back (admin)

Arguments:
  nodes                       node names or ids (default: every online worker
                              that is not current)

Options:
  --now                       do not wait for running jobs: cancel them and
                              update straight away
  --drain-timeout <duration>  explicitly cancel jobs still running after this
                              long (default: wait without cancelling)
  --wait                      follow the rollout until it finishes or halts
  -h, --help                  display help for command

Usage: gridstator agents cancel [options]

Stop the running rollout; the worker being updated right now finishes (admin)

Options:
  -h, --help  display help for command

Usage: gridstator agents set [options] [node]

Set auto-update and toolchain options: for one worker, or the cluster default
(no node)

Arguments:
  node                    node name or id; omit to change the cluster default

Options:
  --auto-update <mode>    off | follow | window, or inherit (node only: use the
                          cluster default)
  --window <HH:MM-HH:MM>  daily update window in the controller’s local time
  --act <version>         act for self-updating workers: a version, "pinned" or
                          "off"
  -h, --help              display help for command

Usage: gridstator build [options] [context]

Build a Docker image from this project on a cluster node (BuildKit)

Arguments:
  context                  build context directory (default: .)

Options:
  -f, --file <Dockerfile>  Dockerfile (default: <context>/Dockerfile)
  -b, --build <name>       use a build defined under `builds:` in gridstator.yml
  --target <stage>         Dockerfile stage to build
  --build-arg <KEY=value>  build argument (repeatable) (default: [])
  -t, --tag <tag>          image tag (repeatable) (default: [])
  --platform <platform>    target platform, e.g. linux/arm64 (repeatable)
                           (default: [])
  --output <mode>          load (into the worker), push, tar (download as
                           artifact) or none
  --no-cache               do not use the build cache
  --pull                   always pull newer base images
  --cache-from <spec>      external cache source, e.g. type=registry,ref=...
                           (repeatable) (default: [])
  --cache-to <spec>        external cache destination (repeatable) (default: [])
  --node <node>            run on this node (name or id)
  --prefer <node>          prefer this worker when it can take the job
                           (repeatable) (default: [])
  -l, --label <label>      require a node label (repeatable) (default: [])
  --cpus <n>               CPUs to reserve
  --memory <size>          memory to reserve, e.g. 8g
  --timeout <duration>     stop the job after this long, e.g. 30m
  --priority <n>           higher runs first (-100..100)
  --name <name>            display name for the job
  -s, --secret-env <NAME>  forward a secret from this shell; masked in logs
                           (repeatable) (default: [])
  -d, --detach             print the job id and exit instead of streaming logs
  --json                   print the submitted job as JSON (implies --detach)
  -h, --help               display help for command

Usage: gridstator actions [options] [command]

Run GitHub Actions workflows on the cluster with act

Options:
  -h, --help                display help for command

Commands:
  list [options]            List workflows and jobs in this project, with
                            local-execution caveats
  run [options] <workflow>  Run a workflow (or one job) against this working
                            tree on a cluster node
  help [command]            display help for command

Usage: gridstator actions list [options]

List workflows and jobs in this project, with local-execution caveats

Options:
  --json      machine-readable output
  -h, --help  display help for command

Usage: gridstator actions run [options] <workflow>

Run a workflow (or one job) against this working tree on a cluster node

Arguments:
  workflow                      workflow file name (ci.yml), path, or name

Options:
  -j, --job <id>                run only this job
  -e, --event <name>            triggering event (default: push, else the first
                                event the workflow declares)
  -i, --input <key=value>       workflow_dispatch input (repeatable) (default:
                                [])
  --var <key=value>             value for the vars context (repeatable)
                                (default: [])
  --env <KEY=value>             environment variable for workflow steps
                                (repeatable) (default: [])
  -P, --platform <label=image>  runner image for a runs-on label (repeatable)
                                (default: [])
  --matrix <key:value>          run only matching matrix combinations
                                (repeatable) (default: [])
  --event-payload <file>        JSON file used as github.event
  --docker-socket               mount the worker's Docker socket into workflow
                                containers
  --node <node>                 run on this node (name or id)
  --prefer <node>               prefer this worker when it can take the job
                                (repeatable) (default: [])
  -l, --label <label>           require a node label (repeatable) (default: [])
  --cpus <n>                    CPUs to reserve
  --memory <size>               memory to reserve, e.g. 8g
  --timeout <duration>          stop the job after this long, e.g. 30m
  --priority <n>                higher runs first (-100..100)
  --name <name>                 display name for the job
  -s, --secret-env <NAME>       forward a secret from this shell; masked in logs
                                (repeatable) (default: [])
  -d, --detach                  print the job id and exit instead of streaming
                                logs
  --json                        print the submitted job as JSON (implies
                                --detach)
  -h, --help                    display help for command

Usage: gridstator artifacts [options] <id>

List or download the artifacts of a job

Arguments:
  id                 job id

Options:
  --download <name>  download this artifact
  -o, --out <path>   where to write the download ("-" for stdout; default: the
                     artifact file name)
  --json             machine-readable output
  -h, --help         display help for command

Usage: gridstator doctor [options]

Check this machine's setup and the connection to the controller

Options:
  --json      machine-readable output
  -h, --help  display help for command

Usage: gridstator controller [options] [command]

Run and manage the cluster controller

Options:
  -h, --help                         display help for command

Commands:
  local                              Manage the controller owned by this account
                                     (used by the VS Code extension)
  init [options]                     Create a new cluster: CA, server
                                     certificate, database and an admin token
  start [options]                    Run the controller in the foreground
  publish-build [options] [tarball]  Publish a verified native release bundle
                                     (manifest and four target archives), drain
                                     the controller and restart (admin)
  token                              Recovery: issue client tokens directly in
                                     the controller database
  install-service [options]          Install an isolated native service: systemd
                                     on Linux, launchd on macOS. User services
                                     start at login; --system starts at boot.
  uninstall-service [options]        Stop and remove the isolated native
                                     controller service (keeps data)
  help [command]                     display help for command

Usage: gridstator controller local [options] [command]

Manage the controller owned by this account (used by the VS Code extension)

Options:
  -h, --help                  display help for command

Commands:
  status [options]            Inspect local ownership, endpoint and user-service
                              state
  ensure-login [options]      Reuse or create one shared local admin login
                              without printing credentials
  service [options] <action>  Control the local controller user service
  configure [options]         Apply a coordinated endpoint change and restart,
                              recovering on failure
  help [command]              display help for command

Usage: gridstator controller local status [options]

Inspect local ownership, endpoint and user-service state

Options:
  --data-dir <dir>  local controller data directory (default:
                    "/TEST_DATA/controller")
  --config <path>   shared client configuration (default:
                    "/TEST_CONFIG/client.json")
  --json            print JSON (local commands always print JSON)
  -h, --help        display help for command

Usage: gridstator controller local ensure-login [options]

Reuse or create one shared local admin login without printing credentials

Options:
  --data-dir <dir>  local controller data directory (default:
                    "/TEST_DATA/controller")
  --config <path>   shared client configuration (default:
                    "/TEST_CONFIG/client.json")
  --json            print JSON (local commands always print JSON)
  --restore         explicitly replace a revoked or expired local login
  -h, --help        display help for command

Usage: gridstator controller local service [options] <action>

Control the local controller user service

Arguments:
  action            start, stop or restart

Options:
  --data-dir <dir>  local controller data directory (default:
                    "/TEST_DATA/controller")
  --config <path>   shared client configuration (default:
                    "/TEST_CONFIG/client.json")
  --json            print JSON (local commands always print JSON)
  -h, --help        display help for command

Usage: gridstator controller local configure [options]

Apply a coordinated endpoint change and restart, recovering on failure

Options:
  --data-dir <dir>  local controller data directory (default:
                    "/TEST_DATA/controller")
  --config <path>   shared client configuration (default:
                    "/TEST_CONFIG/client.json")
  --json            print JSON (local commands always print JSON)
  --host <address>  address to listen on
  --port <port>     TCP port
  --url <url>       HTTPS controller URL reachable by every worker
  -h, --help        display help for command

Usage: gridstator controller init [options]

Create a new cluster: CA, server certificate, database and an admin token

Options:
  --data-dir <dir>  controller data directory (default: "/TEST_DATA/controller")
  --host <host>     address to listen on (default: "0.0.0.0")
  --port <port>     port to listen on (default: "7300")
  --san <names...>  extra hostnames/IPs for the server certificate
  --force           create a new cluster even if one exists (the old data
                    directory is backed up)
  --no-login        do not save the admin credentials as this machine's client
                    configuration
  -h, --help        display help for command

Usage: gridstator controller start [options]

Run the controller in the foreground

Options:
  --data-dir <dir>         controller data directory (default:
                           "/TEST_DATA/controller")
  --host <host>            address to listen on (overrides controller.json)
  --port <port>            port to listen on (overrides controller.json)
  --with-agent             also run a worker agent in this process (embedded
                           mode)
  --agent-name <name>      node name for the embedded agent (default:
                           "<HOSTNAME>")
  --max-concurrency <n>    maximum number of jobs this node runs at once
  --reserve-cpus <n>       CPUs held back for the host (never given to jobs)
  --reserve-memory <size>  memory held back for the host, e.g. 8g
  --labels <list>          comma-separated node labels, e.g. fast,ssd
  -h, --help               display help for command

Usage: gridstator controller publish-build [options] [tarball]

Publish a verified native release bundle (manifest and four target archives),
drain the controller and restart (admin)

Arguments:
  tarball     native release bundle (.tar.gz); defaults to
              GRIDSTATOR_RELEASE_BUNDLE

Options:
  --no-wait   do not wait for the controller to come back on the new build
  -h, --help  display help for command

Usage: gridstator controller token [options] [command]

Recovery: issue client tokens directly in the controller database

Options:
  -h, --help        display help for command

Commands:
  create [options]  Issue a client token without an admin token (needs access to
                    the data directory; works while the controller runs)
  help [command]    display help for command

Usage: gridstator controller token create [options]

Issue a client token without an admin token (needs access to the data directory;
works while the controller runs)

Options:
  --name <name>     token name, e.g. "admin-recovered"
  --role <role>     admin or operator (default: "admin")
  --data-dir <dir>  controller data directory (default: "/TEST_DATA/controller")
  --login           save it as this machine's client login (replaces the current
                    one)
  -h, --help        display help for command

Usage: gridstator controller install-service [options]

Install an isolated native service: systemd on Linux, launchd on macOS. User
services start at login; --system starts at boot.

Options:
  --system             install a system service (needs sudo) instead of a user
                       service
  --user <name>        with --system: the user the service runs as (default: the
                       sudo user)
  --data-dir <dir>     controller data directory
  --print              print the service definition and exit
  --force              replace an existing unit
  --with-agent         also run a worker agent in the controller process
  --agent-name <name>  node name for that agent
  -h, --help           display help for command

Usage: gridstator controller uninstall-service [options]

Stop and remove the isolated native controller service (keeps data)

Options:
  --system    remove the system service instead of the user service
  -h, --help  display help for command

Usage: gridstator agent [options] [command]

Run a worker agent on this machine

Options:
  -h, --help                   display help for command

Commands:
  join [options] <url>         Register this machine with a controller
  start [options]              Run the agent in the foreground
  install-service [options]    Install an isolated native service: systemd on
                               Linux, launchd on macOS. User services start at
                               login; --system starts at boot.
  uninstall-service [options]  Stop and remove the isolated native agent service
                               (keeps data)
  help [command]               display help for command

Usage: gridstator agent join [options] <url>

Register this machine with a controller

Arguments:
  url                      controller URL, e.g. https://192.168.1.20:7300

Options:
  --token <token>          join token from `gridstator token create --join`
  --fingerprint <sha256>   cluster CA fingerprint
  --name <name>            node name (default: "<HOSTNAME>")
  --data-dir <dir>         agent data directory (default: "/TEST_DATA/agent")
  --force                  join again even if this machine already joined a
                           cluster
  --max-concurrency <n>    maximum number of jobs this node runs at once
  --reserve-cpus <n>       CPUs held back for the host (never given to jobs)
  --reserve-memory <size>  memory held back for the host, e.g. 8g
  --labels <list>          comma-separated node labels, e.g. fast,ssd
  -h, --help               display help for command

Usage: gridstator agent start [options]

Run the agent in the foreground

Options:
  --data-dir <dir>         agent data directory (default: "/TEST_DATA/agent")
  --cache-size <size>      maximum snapshot cache size (default: "10g")
  --keep-failed            keep containers and volumes of failed jobs for
                           inspection
  --drain                  on shutdown, wait for running jobs instead of
                           stopping them
  --max-concurrency <n>    maximum number of jobs this node runs at once
  --reserve-cpus <n>       CPUs held back for the host (never given to jobs)
  --reserve-memory <size>  memory held back for the host, e.g. 8g
  --labels <list>          comma-separated node labels, e.g. fast,ssd
  -h, --help               display help for command

Usage: gridstator agent install-service [options]

Install an isolated native service: systemd on Linux, launchd on macOS. User
services start at login; --system starts at boot.

Options:
  --system          install a system service (needs sudo) instead of a user
                    service
  --user <name>     with --system: the user the service runs as (default: the
                    sudo user)
  --data-dir <dir>  agent data directory
  --print           print the service definition and exit
  --force           replace an existing unit
  -h, --help        display help for command

Usage: gridstator agent uninstall-service [options]

Stop and remove the isolated native agent service (keeps data)

Options:
  --system    remove the system service instead of the user service
  -h, --help  display help for command
